cards.text: Just before this, Solomon's heart turned after other gods, and the LORD said He would tear the kingdom away from him. Not in Solomon's lifetime, though, for the sake of his father David. Now trouble starts showing up, and the first name on the list is Hadad the Edomite, from the royal line of Edom.

cards.question: Hadad the Edomite is now Solomon's adversary. Who raised him up against Solomon?

cards.text: Hadad's story starts years earlier. When David was in Edom, Joab, the commander of the army, went to bury the dead.

cards.question: Joab stayed in Edom with all Israel until he had struck down every male in Edom.

cards.text: Six months they stayed. But one young boy got away: Hadad, along with some Edomites who were servants of his father.

cards.question: Where does young Hadad flee with his father's servants?
Hadad and his men go from Midian to Paran, take men from Paran with them, and reach Pharaoh king of Egypt. What does Pharaoh give Hadad?

answers.text: A house and land and food
A post in his royal army
A ship to sail back home

cards.text: Friend, the best real estate I ever got in my junk drawer was the spot under a takeout menu, and Hadad gets a HOUSE. It gets better: Hadad finds great favor in Pharaoh's sight.

cards.question: Pharaoh gives Hadad a wife: the ___ of Queen Tahpenes, Pharaoh's own wife.

cards.text: Hadad and his wife have a son named Genubath. Queen Tahpenes herself weans him in Pharaoh's palace.

cards.question: Genubath lives in Pharaoh's palace among the sons of Pharaoh.
In Egypt, Hadad hears that David has rested with his fathers and that Joab is dead. What does Hadad ask Pharaoh?

answers.text: To let him return to his own country
To give him soldiers to fight Israel
To let Genubath rule over Edom

cards.text: I bet Pharaoh's jaw drops. He asks, 'What have you lacked here with me that you suddenly want to go back to your own country?'

cards.question: Pharaoh asks Hadad what he has lacked in Egypt. How does Hadad answer?

answers.text: He lacked nothing but still wants to go
He misses his father's people in Edom
He fears Pharaoh will turn against him

cards.text: That's like quitting the best job you ever had, and when the boss asks what's wrong, you just say, 'Nothing.' And Hadad isn't the only one, because God raises up another adversary against Solomon.

cards.question: The new adversary is Rezon son of Eliada, who had fled from his ___, Hadadezer king of Zobah.

cards.text: Rezon gathers men to himself. When David killed the Zobaites, Rezon captained a band of raiders.

cards.question: Where does Rezon's band of raiders go to settle and gain control?
Once Solomon is king, Rezon makes peace with Israel.

cards.text: Rezon rules over Aram, Israel's enemy all through Solomon's days, adding to the trouble caused by Hadad. Solomon's calendar is filling up with people who are mad at him.
Now meet the third name, and this one comes from inside Israel. Jeroboam son of Nebat, an Ephraimite from Zeredah, whose mother is a widow named Zeruah.

cards.question: Jeroboam is one of Solomon's own servants.

cards.text: And this servant rebels against the king. It starts back when Solomon had built the supporting terraces and repaired the gap in the wall of the city of his father David.

cards.question: Solomon notices that Jeroboam, a mighty man of valor, is an industrious young man. What does Solomon do with him?

answers.text: Puts him over the labor force of Joseph's house
Makes him commander of the whole army
Sends him to rebuild the walls of Gezer

cards.text: Hard worker, big promotion. I've been running this bakery for ages and nobody's promoted me yet, probably because I'd have to do it myself.
Then the prophet Ahijah the Shilonite meets Jeroboam on the road out of Jerusalem. Ahijah's wrapped in a new cloak, and the two of them are alone in the open field.

cards.question: Alone in the field, what does Ahijah do with his new cloak?

answers.text: Spreads it out on the road

cards.text: He tore up a brand NEW cloak, friend, not the old one, the NEW one! Then Ahijah tells Jeroboam, 'Take ten pieces for yourself,' because this is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says.

cards.question: Ten pieces of cloak for Jeroboam, because the LORD says He will give him ten ___.
The LORD says one tribe will remain. Why?

answers.text: For the sake of David and Jerusalem
Because Solomon will turn back to Him
Because Jeroboam will ask for mercy

cards.text: Then the LORD says why the kingdom is being torn. They have forsaken Him to worship Ashtoreth of the Sidonians, Chemosh of the Moabites and Milcom of the Ammonites.

cards.question: The LORD says they have kept His statutes and judgments as Solomon's father David did.
The LORD won't take the whole kingdom out of Solomon's hand. How long will Solomon stay ruler?

answers.text: All the days of his life

cards.text: That's for the sake of David, whom the LORD chose because he kept His commandments and statutes.

cards.question: The ten tribes will be taken from the hand of Solomon's ___ and given to Jeroboam.

cards.text: One tribe goes to Solomon's son, so that David will always have a lamp before the LORD in Jerusalem, the city where He chose to put His Name.
Ahijah is still out in that field with Jeroboam, passing along what the LORD says. Now the LORD's words turn to Jeroboam himself.

cards.question: What does the LORD promise Jeroboam?

answers.text: He will be king over Israel
He will be a prophet like Ahijah
He will lead Solomon's whole army

cards.text: But there's an IF. If Jeroboam listens to all the LORD commands, walks in His ways and does what is right as David did, then the LORD will be with him.

cards.question: If Jeroboam obeys, the LORD will build him a lasting ___ just as He built for David.
The LORD says He will humble David's descendants forever.

cards.text: Humbled, but not forever. So Solomon seeks to kill Jeroboam.

cards.question: Jeroboam runs for his life. Where does he flee?

cards.text: Jeroboam goes to Shishak, king of Egypt, and stays there until Solomon dies. Same country young Hadad ran to, so Egypt is basically this chapter's waiting room.
As for the rest of what Solomon did, and his wisdom, it's all written in the Book of the Acts of Solomon.

cards.question: Solomon reigned in Jerusalem over all Israel for ___ years.
Solomon rests with his fathers and is buried in the city of his father David. Who reigns in his place?

cards.text: And that's where we set this batch down for now. Trust me, friend, this kingdom story is NOT done.

findings.problem: The card cites 1 Kings 11:11-14, but its first claim, that Solomon's heart turned after other gods, comes from 1 Kings 11:4 (and 11:9), not 11:11-13. The citation doesn't start at the first verse the card uses.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The opening card says the tearing won't happen in Solomon's lifetime, for the sake of his father David. That gives away the answer to stop 2 card 13 (Solomon stays ruler 'All the days of his life'). It also points straight at the right answer to stop 2 card 10 (one tribe remains 'For the sake of David and Jerusalem').

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: This story card only recaps card 4's answer ('Hard worker, big promotion') and adds a joke. It cites 11:28, which card 4 already covered, and tells no new part of the passage. The joke isn't riding on a card that moves the passage forward.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage. No recap cards. Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: The setup says they have forsaken the LORD to worship Ashtoreth, Chemosh and Milcom. Card 12 then asks whether they kept His statutes and judgments as David did. The setup already rules out 'True', so the card tests nothing the baker has to reason out.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.
